subject: Re: Unexpected mid-quarter surge — proposal to convert burst pool to committed GPUs
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah@avacloud.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-quarter surge: can we convert our burst pool into committed capacity?

Hi Irene,

Quick context: we launched a targeted paid campaign last week and are seeing sustained 2.6x token throughput vs our forecast. The burst GPU pool we bought is being consumed quickly and the team is worried about throttling for customer-facing features. Procurement asked whether we can convert a portion of the burst pool into committed capacity for the remainder of the contract period so we avoid repeated top-ups.

Can your team run a short utilization analysis and propose a conversion option (e.g., 8 GPUs committed now, with a 30-day review)? Also need the commercial delta for committed vs burst pricing and any SLA implications. I attached our Q3 usage extract.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sr. SRE, AvaCloud

Attachment: avacloud-utilization-q3-dashboard.csv

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Li <sarah@avacloud.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter surge: can we convert our burst pool into committed capacity?

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. We"d like to propose a pragmatic, low-risk approach:

- Quick triage: our infra team (Ben) will validate the CSV and produce a 7-day projected utilization curve.
- Tactical conversion: convert 8 GPUs to a short-term committed tranche, with a 30-day usage review and an option to scale up or unwind.
- Commercials: committed GPUs have a lower per-token effective cost and bring SLA guarantees vs burst credits; commercial delta will be scoped once Ben validates average sustained utilization.

I"ll loop Vanessa for the renewal/commercials side. Do you have an internal procurement contact we should include?

Irene
Head of Dedicated Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Sarah Li <sarah@avacloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter surge: can we convert our burst pool into committed capacity?

Following up with the utilization triage. I ran the supplied CSV plus the last 48h of telemetry from the serving runtime. Key findings:

- Sustained 24-hour moving average shows 2.1x baseline for the last 5 days.
- Peak windows are predictable: 11:00-14:00 PST and 19:00-21:00 PST.
- Current burst pool consumption would exhaust available credits in ~12 days if trend continues.

Recommendation (technical):
1) Convert 8 GPUs now to committed tranches (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) and configure smart routing so low-latency customer requests use committed instances while background async jobs continue on burst.
2) Enable prefix caching for high-frequency prompts to reduce token churn across peak windows.
3) Configure a 30-day review with automatic rollback trigger if average utilization drops below 1.2x baseline for a rolling 14-day window.

I attached a condensed CSV of projected utilization and a short config snippet for routing rules. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the numbers.

-Ben
Lead Solutions Engineer
Attachment: avacloud-utilization-q3-dashboard-condensed.csv

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Li <sarah@avacloud.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter surge: proposal and commercial sketch

Sarah — appreciate the fast data. Commercial sketch below (high level):

- Option A (3-month buffer): Commit 8 GPUs for the next 3 months at the committed rate; 20% discount vs equivalent burst consumption over the same period; includes 99.9% uptime SLA and prioritized capacity.
- Option B (30-day trial + convert): Commit 8 GPUs for 30 days; at day 30 either convert to 3-month commit or unwind. Priced pro-rata with one-time conversion admin fee.
- Add-on: we can reserve a 2-GPU warm buffer for peak bursts (billed as low-util standby) to absorb unexpected spikes during evaluation window.

Before we finalize numbers, two asks:
1) Can you confirm procurement contact and billing cadence?
2) Are you able to commit to the 30-day review cadence for the trial?

I attached a proposed phased tranche spreadsheet that shows the monthly delta and token-effective price. If this looks reasonable we"ll produce a formal amendment to the contract and update the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-phased-tranche.xlsx

From: Sarah Li <sarah@avacloud.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter surge: proposal and commercial sketch

Thanks Vanessa, Ben, Irene — this looks good and much appreciated. Procurement (procurement@avacloud.com) confirms Option B (30-day trial) is ideal. Billing cadence: monthly invoicing; procurement will sign the amendment if the trial includes the 2-GPU warm buffer and the rollback trigger you outlined.

Next steps we agree on:
- Redwood sends contract amendment for the 30-day trial (8 committed GPUs + 2 warm buffer) by EOD 9/3.
- Ben to provision committed tranche and configure routing rules; provide verification runbook.
- Joint review scheduled for 30 days after provisioning (tentative: 10/3).

If you can send the amendment and a short runbook link, procurement will route for approval.

Regards,
Sarah
Sr. SRE, AvaCloud
Cc: procurement@avacloud.com
